claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few key questions:

**What are the names and ages of the children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**First, is Alex still in full-time education, or are they working/not in education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Alex being in full-time education is important for Child Benefit eligibility at that age.

**Next, I need to know: Are you the parent or guardian with primary responsibility for Alex, and do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and he lives at home with me. And yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's useful to know.

**Now, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, have you lived in the UK for at least 2 of the last 3 years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I've lived here my whole life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**One more important question: What is your current residency status? Are you living in the UK at the moment, or are you temporarily abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living in the UK at the moment, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that confirmation.

**Just to clarify one more thing: Is Alex receiving any other state benefits in his own right, such as Income Support or Jobseeker's Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**One final question: Does anyone else claim Child Benefit for Alex, or have you claimed it before for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 17 years old and in full-time education (A-levels at college)
- You are Alex's parent with primary responsibility and he lives with you
- You are a British citizen who has lived in the UK your whole life
- You are currently residing in the UK
- Alex is not receiving other state benefits
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Let me determine your eligibility:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Your eligibility is confirmed because:
- Alex is 17 years old and in full-time education, which means he qualifies even though he's over 16
- You are his parent with primary responsibility and he lives with you
- You are a British citizen currently residing in the UK
- All other eligibility requirements are met

If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
